September 29, 2026 | 🟢

<u>NYT</u>: A Former President's Son Poses a Test for Mexico's Governing Party
September 29, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Paywalled, but the headline says enough: the NYT makes AMLO's son, not any charge or ruling, the "test" for Mexico's governing party. It lands six weeks after Washington revoked his US visa without public explanation.

🇲🇽 The State Department still hasn't given a public reason for the visa revocation, and no Mexican court has charged him with anything.

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico ships AI hardware with just 7% Mexican content. Goal: 40%</u>

Mexico's computer exports to the US are booming on the AI build-out, but Mexican value added is only 7–8%: processors, memory and advanced chips come from Taiwan, China, Malaysia and Korea. "Our task is for value added to go to 30 or 40% in the coming years, hand in hand with the US and Canada," Deputy Trade Minister Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez told El Economista. Autos already carry 35% Mexican content. Next up is a national semiconductor design center.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Zapopan's poisoned waterfall: Morena takes Huaxtla to federal authorities</u>

Morena in Zapopan, Jalisco, is asking Profepa and Conagua to audit the landfill runoff from the Picachos and Hasar's dumps that has turned the turquoise Huaxtla waterfalls and the Milpillas river a dull ochre. Barranca communities (Milpillas, Huaxtla, San Lorenzo, Mesa de San Juan, Ixcatán) have been reporting it to municipal, state and federal authorities since 2009 without any answer. Seventeen years of leachate under a municipal government now led by MC's Juan José Frangie.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>PAN's Maru Campos asks the Supreme Court to save her "narco" election law</u>

Chihuahua's PAN governor María Eugenia Campos is pressing the SCJN to uphold her state reform that lets authorities annul an election if organized crime intervenes and bars candidates "linked" to crime. Morena challenged it in court: its lawmakers argue it lets people be punished on suspicion alone, without evidence, trampling the presumption of innocence. Campos pitches it as "what no other state dared to do," one year before Chihuahua picks her successor, and days after the US ambassador publicly backed her.

🇲🇽💼 <u>60.7 million Mexicans at work: 1.3 million more in a year</u>

Mexico's employed population hit 60.7 million in August, 1.3 million more than August 2025 and the highest ever for that month, Labor Secretary Marath Bolaños reported. Women's labor participation reached 41%, up 2.2 points. And 199,454 app-platform workers have now crossed the income threshold into full social security, while 1.77 million got workplace-accident coverage, including people who drive "once a week or an hour a day."
banner: JOBS: 1.3 MILLION MORE IN A YEAR

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>AHMSA bidder vows to restart Monclova steel in six months</u>

The idle Altos Hornos de México steelworks may finally have a buyer. José Arturo Domínguez of CIESA, one of six qualified bidders, says he is "not a front man" and that his money will go to reactivating the Monclova plant and its Minosa mining arm, not to creditors or the government, with operations back in roughly six months. His offer topped the auction's reference price by about $272.6 million. Thousands of Coahuila steelworkers are waiting to see if the furnaces actually relight.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Infonavit cuts up to 90,000 pesos off Bienestar homes for the lowest earners</u>

Starting today, Infonavit applies a sliding discount on first sales of Vivienda para el Bienestar homes: workers earning 1 to 2.09 minimum wages get up to 90,000 pesos off, falling 10,000 pesos per bracket to zero at 2.9 minimum wages. The price cap is set at 862,000 pesos, for households earning under three minimum wages.
banner: INFONAVIT: UP TO 90K PESOS OFF HOMES

text:
🇲🇽📊 <u>GENDER PAY GAP: FROM 20% TO 14% IN TWO DECADES</u>

According to El Economista, the income gap between men and women in Mexico fell from 20% in 2005 to about 14% in 2025, just six points in 20 years. Part of the reason: 54-55% of working women are in the informal economy, where minimum-wage increases don't reach them. Women also do 40-42 hours a week of unpaid care work, compared with 15-17 for men. Women hold just 3% of general-director posts.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NUEVO LEÓN OWES THE PEOPLE 6.29 BILLION PESOS</u>

The Federal Administrative Court (TFJA) unanimously upheld the SAT's 6,292-million-peso tax claim against Nuevo León's government for income-tax withholdings the state never handed over to the federation. The debt began in 2020 under Jaime "El Bronco" Rodríguez, who refused to pay, and kept growing under Samuel García, even after a ruling that would have wiped it out was overturned. The state can still appeal to a circuit court or the Supreme Court.
banner: NUEVO LEÓN: 6.29 BN PESOS OWED TO SAT
